Why we write slowly

Mira Patel
March 12 · 6 min read

Most of what we write at work is written fast: a reply, a ticket, a summary nobody asked for. Speed is a fine habit for messages and a poor one for decisions, which is why the best teams we know keep a slower kind of writing alongside the quick one.

Writing slowly is thinking with the brakes on, so you notice the turns.

Slow writing is not long writing. A good planning note is often shorter than the chat thread it replaces, because the work happened before the words did. Read more in our guide to planning notes.
